assertion_results.text: Data extraction correctly identifies CVE-2026-31812, library quinn-proto, affected range < 0.11.14, and fixed version 0.11.14 from the Vulnerability issue (Step 1)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Step 1 table: CVE ID = CVE-2026-31812, Vulnerable library = quinn-proto, Affected version range = 'versions before 0.11.14 (< 0.11.14)', Fixed version = 0.11.14. All four fields correctly extracted.

assertion_results.text: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as Cargo based on the library name and component context (Step 1 Ecosystem detection)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Ecosystem Detection section: 'The vulnerable library quinn-proto is a Rust crate. The ecosystem is Cargo, which is a source dependency ecosystem. The lock file is Cargo.lock'. Correctly identifies Cargo ecosystem.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the security-matrix.md supportability matrix — no versions are skipped (Important Rule 4)
assertion_results.evidence: security-matrix-mock.md defines 7 versions: 2.1.0, 2.1.1 (stream 2.1.x) and 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 2.2.4 (stream 2.2.x). version-impact.md table contains all 7 versions with matching build tags (v0.3.8, v0.3.12, v0.4.5, v0.4.8, v0.4.9, v0.4.11, v0.4.12). No versions skipped.

assertion_results.text: Version impact analysis uses pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version, not branch HEAD (Important Rule 13)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md Build Tag column uses pinned tags from the supportability matrix: v0.3.8, v0.3.12, v0.4.5, v0.4.8, v0.4.9, v0.4.11, v0.4.12. Evidence section states: 'All quinn-proto versions were extracted from Cargo.lock at the pinned source commits listed in the supportability matrix.' Tags match security-matrix-mock.md backend column exactly.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table identifies retag versions and carries forward the affected status from the original version (Important Rule 5)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md row for 2.2.2: Build Tag v0.4.9, quinn-proto '--', Affected 'YES', Notes 'retag of 2.2.1 (same as v0.4.8: quinn-proto 0.11.12)'. The retag is identified, quinn-proto value is not independently looked up (shown as --), and affected status YES is carried forward from 2.2.1. Matches security-matrix-mock.md which marks v0.4.9 as 'backend retag of 2.2.1'.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction proposes replacing PSIRT-assigned versions with lock-file-verified versions, showing the diff (Step 3.2)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md shows Current vs. Proposed table: Current (PSIRT-assigned) = 'RHTPA 2.0.0', Proposed (lock file evidence) = 'RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2'. Proposed Comment shows diff: 'Corrected Affects Versions: [RHTPA 2.0.0] -> [RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2].' Each proposed version is justified with lock file evidence showing quinn-proto versions at pinned commits.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction references version names from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md uses version names 'RHTPA 2.2.0', 'RHTPA 2.2.1', 'RHTPA 2.2.2' throughout. The Jira API call uses placeholder IDs '<jira-id-for-RHTPA-2.2.0>' etc., with explicit note: 'Jira version IDs would be discovered dynamically via getJiraIssueTypeMetaWithFields (Step 3.1), not hardcoded.' No numeric Jira version IDs are hardcoded.

assertion_results.text: Remediation tasks include Repository, Target Branch, acceptance criteria, and dependency linkage between upstream and downstream tasks (Important Rule 9)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Task 1: Repository = rhtpa-backend, Target Branch = release/0.4.z, Acceptance Criteria with 4 checkboxes, Dependencies = TC-8001. Task 2: Repository = rhtpa-release.0.4.z, Target Branch = main, Acceptance Criteria with 2 checkboxes, Dependencies = 'dependency bump task (upstream fix must merge first)' and TC-8001. Linkage table shows 'Blocks | Task 1 (dependency bump) | Task 2 (downstream propagation)'. All four required elements present.

assertion_results.text: For Cargo ecosystem, remediation creates two tasks: upstream backport task and downstream propagation subtask with Blocks dependency (Important Rule 8)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md creates Task 1 (Dependency Bump for 2.2.x) and Task 2 (Downstream Propagation for 2.2.x) for the scoped stream - 2 tasks. Linkage Summary shows 'Blocks | Task 1 (dependency bump) | Task 2 (downstream propagation)'. Task 2 Link field: 'Blocks (Task 1 inward, this task outward)'. Similarly for 2.1.x preemptive stream: Task 3 (upstream backport) and Task 4 (downstream propagation) with 'Blocks | Task 3 (upstream backport) | Task 4 (downstream propagation)'.

assertion_results.text: The analysis presents triage recommendations as proposed actions — framing Affects Versions changes, label additions, and status transitions as proposals rather than executed mutations (Guardrails)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md: 'Actions (would be performed via Jira MCP):', 'No Jira operations were performed (eval-only mode).' affects-versions.md: '## Proposed Jira Update', '## Proposed Comment', 'No Jira operations were performed (eval-only mode).' remediation.md: 'Would be posted to TC-8001', 'Would add the ai-cve-triaged label', 'If accepted, would create:', 'No Jira operations were performed (eval-only mode).' All actions consistently framed as proposals, not executed mutations.

assertion_results.text: The data-extraction output describes Step 0.7 actions before the Step 1 data table: assigning the CVE issue to the current user and transitioning it to Assigned status (Step 0.7)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md lines 1-28: '# Step 0.7 -- Early Assignment Actions' appears first, describing (1) assigning TC-8001 to current user via jira.edit_issue, (2) discovering Assigned transition via jira.get_transitions, (3) transitioning from New to Assigned via jira.transition_issue. Lines 30+: '# Step 1 -- Data Extraction' follows. Step 0.7 correctly precedes Step 1.

assertion_results.text: Release orchestration preserves interactive confirmation of the exact release Epic version and separate child Task creation; when release evidence or confirmation is unavailable, it reports pending work instead of claiming creation.
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Step 7.5.1: presents 'Confirmation required:' block with three options (Accept, Specify different version, Skip). Uses conditional language: 'If no existing release Epic is found', 'If accepted, would create:'. Step 7.5.2: 'If no release Task exists, would create:'. Epic and Task creation are described as separate steps (7.5.1 and 7.5.2). No creation is claimed as executed - all framed as pending work requiring confirmation.

assertion_results.text: Release dedup is skipped when its Upstream Affected Component configuration is absent. When trusted release evidence is available, the proposed procedure resolves originating CVEs through Blocks/Depend links, compares their components and allows library-summary fallback only for a missing Depend link or component field; a known nonmatch does not count as dedup, and unavailable release evidence is not fabricated.
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Step 7.5.3: 'Result: SKIPPED. The Upstream Affected Component custom field is not configured in the project's Security Configuration. Without this field, cross-CVE dedup cannot be performed. Proceeding to Step 8 without dedup filtering.' Dedup is correctly skipped due to absent configuration. No release evidence is fabricated. No dedup matching is attempted or claimed.
